item.title: Why the US Needs to Rethink Its Hopes for Saudi Arabia
item.description: Despite many US inducements, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has turned away from normalization with Israel and broader US alignment in the Middle East. The post Why the US Needs to Rethink Its Hopes for Saudi Arabia appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: China’s Silent Nuclear Warning to Russia: The New Type 096 Submarine
item.description: At its current production rates, China is likely to have a far more menacing submarine force than Russia in short order—though its quality is still uncertain. The post China’s Silent Nuclear Warning to Russia: The New Type 096 Submarine appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Iran’s Digital Blackout Reveals About Cyber Power
item.description: The United States should partner with Israel on cyber power as authoritarian regimes refine digital control faster than democratic governance frameworks are emerging. Recent protests in Iran illustrate how control over digital infrastructure can be converted directly into control over society, and how this lesson is being closely observed by America’s adversaries. item.title: Is the Dassault Rafale the Best Non-American Air-to-Air Fighter?
item.description: The Dassault Rafale is neatly tailored to France’s aerial doctrine—namely an ability to carry out missions independently, with limited logistical or ISR support. The post Is the Dassault Rafale the Best Non-American Air-to-Air Fighter? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Move Over, James Bond: Russia Has a New “PPK”—and It’s a Lot Bigger
item.description: Unlike Bond’s weapon of choice, the Russian PPK-20 is a new submachine gun with an estimated firing rate of 800 rounds per minute. The post Move Over, James Bond: Russia Has a New “PPK”—and It’s a Lot Bigger appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Europe’s Meteor vs. America’s AMRAAM: Which Is the Better Missile?
item.description: Though the two air-to-air missiles are broadly similar, one has a decisive advantage in aerial kills, thanks to its far larger “no-escape zone.” The post Europe’s Meteor vs. America’s AMRAAM: Which Is the Better Missile? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How the Soviet Union’s Mi-8 Helicopter Took Over the Developing World
item.description: The Mi-8 is far more cost-competitive than Western counterparts, and focuses on redundancy and ease of use rather than exacting performance standards. The post How the Soviet Union’s Mi-8 Helicopter Took Over the Developing World appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The 10 Most Commonly Exported Fighter Jets
